response:
Diagnosis after generation 4. Two designs now sit at the frontier with *different* strengths: the gen-1 industry-neutral composite has the best cross-sectional slope (fmb −4.20, alpha −3.7%, t=−2.98, Sharpe −0.47), while the gen-4 hybrid frame (industry-neutral accruals × own-history issuance percentile) matches its alpha and delivers the best Sharpe (−0.53) with a much weaker slope (−2.29). This is a real economic tension, not noise: cross-sectional issuance ranks capture *type* (chronically capital-hungry firms), which is what a pooled FMB regression rewards, while own-history ranks capture *events* (an unusual raise), which produces a cleaner, better-diversified portfolio spread. Two further gen-4 results were leg-level improvements that have never been used together: adding depreciation back to isolate working-capital accruals (fmb −3.81, alpha −3.3%, t=−2.68) and measuring financing net of internal earnings (fmb −3.41, alpha −2.9%, Sharpe −0.42). This batch therefore (i) fuses the two normalization frames so the financing leg carries both type and event information, (ii) stacks the two validated leg refinements, (iii) tests a robustness choice (industry ranks vs z-scores) that could stabilize the portfolio, and (iv) explores two untested financing actions: revolver-funded working-capital buildups and payout distributed in excess of earnings.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: DualFrameFinancingAccruals
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at)), TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Accrual-heavy firms are most mispriced when they are both structurally dependent on outside capital (high versus industry peers) and raising unusually much versus their own funding history, because the first identifies the vulnerable business model and the second identifies the opportunistic event.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The archive's two frontier signals differ only in how the financing leg is normalized, and each dominates a different metric, which implies the two frames carry complementary information rather than substituting for each other. Averaging them inside the financing leg keeps the accrual leg at full 50% weight, so this should recover the strong FMB slope of the cross-sectional version while retaining the superior Sharpe of the event version.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: WCAccrualsWithIssuanceBeyondEarnings
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), dpc), at)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), ib), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: The sharpest version of the story is a working-capital-driven earnings overstatement funded by capital raised well in excess of what the firm actually earned — discretionary accounting on the asset side, opportunistic financing on the liability side.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Generation 4 validated each leg refinement separately against the same benchmark — depreciation add-back on the accrual side and internal-funds-relative scaling on the financing side — but never jointly, so this tests whether their improvements are additive or overlapping. Both refinements sharpen the economic content rather than the statistics, so if they are independent the composite should exceed the gen-1 benchmark on both slope and alpha.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: IndRankAccrualFinancing
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: The economic content of the interaction is ordinal — being an accrual-aggressive, capital-raising firm relative to peers — so within-industry percentile ranks should represent it more robustly than z-scores, which are distorted by the extreme scaled ratios of small, low-asset firms.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: IND_ZSCORE standardizes by an industry standard deviation that is itself dominated by a handful of extreme observations, which can make the tails of the sorted portfolio unstable and depress ls_talpha relative to the underlying slope. This is a deliberate single-choice isolation of the standardization operator on the archive's best signal, and its outcome tells later generations whether outlier control or economic content is the binding constraint on portfolio evidence.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: WCAccrualsFundedByShortTermDebt
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), dpc), at)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(DELTA(dlc, 1), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Working-capital accruals financed by an increase in current debt represent the most fragile funding structure: long-duration, illiquid receivables and inventory financed with claims that come due within a year.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The financing legs tested so far are either total volumes or maturity *shares*; the actual flow of new short-term borrowing has only appeared inside a failed multi-leg construction, and it is the funding source that must be rolled precisely when accruals reverse. Pairing it with the depreciation-adjusted accrual leg matches the asset and liability sides of the same economic mismatch.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: AccrualsWithPayoutBeyondEarnings
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dvt, prstkc), ib), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Distributing more cash to shareholders than the firm earned, while earnings are already accrual-inflated, indicates a payout being sustained by outside capital or balance-sheet depletion rather than by real profits.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The earlier payout test measured only the *absence* of distributions and was weak, but over-distribution relative to reported earnings is the economically opposite and much more informative condition, since it forces the firm back to the capital markets. This keeps the proven accrual leg fixed so the test cleanly evaluates a payout-sustainability channel that the issuance-volume legs cannot capture.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: SymmetricDualFrameAccrualFinancing
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 5)), SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at)), TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Both accounting aggressiveness and financing dependence should be judged simultaneously against peers and against the firm's own history, so that the signal fires on firms that are both structurally low-quality and currently deviating from their own norm on both dimensions.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Own-history normalization of the accrual leg was only tested in isolation, where it weakened the slope (fmb −1.87) but delivered a strong Sharpe (−0.49), suggesting it adds event information while discarding level information; combining rather than substituting the frames should retain both. Paired with Signal 1, this determines whether the accrual leg benefits from dual framing or whether only the financing leg does.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
